description: Registry of known flaky tests. Each entry documents a test that has exhibited non-deterministic failure, either currently active or resolved. Active entries inform CI triage; resolved entries are retained as institutional memory.

fields.subsystem: Logical subsystem: parser | lsp | dap | workspace | semantic | lexer | ux
fields.failure_mode: Brief description of the non-determinism (race condition, timing, env-dependent, etc.)
fields.issue: GitHub issue number that tracked the flakiness
fields.first_seen: ISO 8601 date of first observed failure
fields.resolved_in: PR number that fixed the flakiness (only for resolved entries)
fields.resolved_at: ISO 8601 date resolved (only for resolved entries)

entries.failure_mode: Nondeterministic + duplicate output: the folding-range provider emits each subroutine fold twice (no dedup across passes) and computes a nondeterministic start line for the second #region fold (observed startLine 6 vs the expected 7), so the test's region-fold filter only matches on ~1/3 of runs. Inside the merge-blocking unit_routed_full gate (pr-smoke), this single flake throttled the entire merge queue.
entries.notes: Fixed by deduplicating folding ranges at the response-assembly seam and correcting the test's expected region-start-line from 7 to 6 (# region Main Logic is on line 6).

entries.failure_mode: Timing-sensitive: rapid event batching window occasionally expired before the assertion fired on loaded CI runners, producing a spurious 'expected 1 notification, got 2' failure.
entries.notes: Fixed by widening the debounce assertion window from 10ms to 50ms and adding a jitter-tolerant retry loop in the test harness.
